subject: Batch job completion windows & idempotency — SLA exception request
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datahype.io>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@datahype.io, Anya K. <anya.k@datahype.io>
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA exception for nightly bulk scoring jobs

Hi Rishi,

Quick context: we’re evaluating Redwood for our production inference layer for batch scoring (50M records/night). Our procurement and engineering teams reviewed the standard SLA (99.9% uptime for online endpoints) but we need explicit coverage for long-running asynchronous jobs — completion window guarantees and retry/idempotency behavior.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood commit to a job completion window (e.g., 24 hours) for scheduled night runs, with SLO credits if exceeded?
- What are the retry semantics and idempotency guarantees for async job requeues? We need to be confident that retries won’t cause duplicate side effects downstream.

We’re tight on our go-live timeline, so can we get a short exception or addendum that covers these batch semantics while legal finalizes the master services agreement?

Attaching a short matrix of expected behavior.

Thanks —
Oliver
Head of Data Platform
DataHype Analytics
[Attachment: batch_job_sla_matrix.pdf (pdf)]

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datahype.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for nightly bulk scoring jobs

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear summary and the matrix. We're excited about DataHype moving forward. Quick responses to your two asks, and I've looped Marcus (solutions) and Laura (sales lead) to align on commercial terms.

1) Completion window: We can offer a contractual completion SLO for scheduled batch jobs. Typical commitments we’ve done are 24 hours for very large nightly runs, with a financial credit tier if not met. We'll need: average job size (records & tokens), typical peak concurrency, and whether jobs are prioritized or preemptible.

2) Retries & idempotency: Our async runner supports exactly-once semantics for outputs when customers provide a stable job_id + idempotency token. Retries are attempted automatically up to N times (configurable; default 3) with exponential backoff. Important caveats below from Marcus on side effects.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to provide the technical behavior we recommend (idempotency token use, effective TTLs, canonical retry window).
- I'll draft a short SLA exception addendum (30-day temporary effective period) for procurement to review; Laura can flag commercial credit bands.

Can you share: nightly job estimate (records) and whether the jobs write to downstream systems (DBs, pub/sub) that cannot tolerate duplicates?

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datahype.io>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for nightly bulk scoring jobs

On Sun, Aug 3, 2025 at 11:03 AM rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> 2) Retries & idempotency: Our async runner supports exactly-once semantics for outputs when customers provide a stable job_id + idempotency token. Retries are attempted automatically up to N times (configurable; default 3) with exponential backoff. Important caveats below from Marcus on side effects.

Oliver / team — details from infra/solutions:
- Job completion window: For very large jobs (50M records), completion depends on effective batching, model token lengths, and throughput profile. We generally surface a completion SLO as a function: max(T_base, k * records / effective_throughput). Practically we've committed to 24hr windows where customers accept:
  * shardable job input (line-delimited records or chunked blobs),
  * retry-friendly processing (idempotency tokens per record or per output key), and
  * visibility hooks (per-shard status webhooks + per-job trace ids).
- Idempotency and side effects: Redwood ensures idempotent scoring outputs when: a) the client-provided job_id is stable across retries, and b) the client either (1) uses our output-assurance API that writes results to a versioned storage object (object name includes job_id + shard_id + attempt), or (2) accepts our at-least-once delivery but handles dedupe downstream. We cannot guarantee suppression of external side effects unless writes go through our managed output-assurance path.
- Retries: default behavior is 3 attempts with 2^n * 2s backoff. Customers can set max_attempts and a retry cut-off (e.g., 18 hours after start). If a job exceeds the configured retry window, it's marked failed and a partial-results package is produced.
- Recommended config for DataHype (50M/night):
  * job_id: stable string provided by DataHype
  * shard_size: 100k records
  * output path: s3://datahype-redwood/results/{job_id}/{shard_id}/attempt-{n}.json
  * retry_window: 18 hours (we can expand to 24 for SLA purposes)
  * monitoring hooks: enable per-shard webhook + enable long-poll status API

I'll attach a short internal notes doc for the SLA team to reference. If DataHype needs Redwood to take responsibility for duplicate suppression to external systems (DB writes, downstream pub/sub), that would require implementing our managed commit API (and would be scoped in the addendum).

— Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sla-exception-form.docx (docx)]

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datahype.io>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2025 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for nightly bulk scoring jobs

Oliver — appreciate the detail. Commercially, we are willing to sign a 30-day SLA exception addendum that:
- Provides a 24-hour contractual completion SLO for scheduled nightly bulk jobs (up to 60M records) with a single-tier credit equal to 10% of that month's usage for missed windows.
- Includes the recommended retry_window and shard settings from Marcus.
- Requires DataHype to use the job_id + output-assurance API OR opt into Redwood-managed commit for downstream dedupe (additional professional services fee applies).

Next steps:
- Rishi will share the draft addendum (we'll include start/end dates).
- Procurement to return a signed PO or redlines.

I'll hold the exception pending final PO; Rishi — please loop legal if they want to widen credit tiers.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datahype.io>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@datahype.io, Anya K. <anya.k@datahype.io>
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for nightly bulk scoring jobs

Laura / Rishi / Marcus — this is good progress. We accept the 24-hour completion SLO and the 10% single-tier credit for missed windows as an interim measure. A couple of quick clarifications before we sign the addendum:

1) Can the completion SLO be limited to scheduled jobs initiated via the Redwood scheduler (we don’t want ad-hoc API batch runs included).
2) For managed commit path: can you provide an estimate of the implementation timeline and any one-time PS cost?

We are attaching a provisional PO and would like to align on dates: go-live target 2025-09-01. If you can get the draft addendum to procurement today we’ll review and circulate redlines.

Thanks —
Oliver
Head of Data Platform
DataHype Analytics
[Attachment: DataHype_Provisional_PO.pdf (pdf)]
